correctness.rationale: Normalized adjacency Fourier fiber is [[2 cosθ/3,1/sqrt3],[1/sqrt3,0]], with eigenvalues (c±sqrt(c²+3))/3 and normalized positive lower-band u(c). Spectrum of normalized Laplacian is [0,2/3]∪[4/3,2]. For 0<ω≤4/3 the spectral subspace has fiber dimension one almost everywhere, and the frame multiplier is |<w,u(c)>|². The two endpoint vectors v,q have positive overlap s<1; averaging their squared projections upper-bounds any sensor by (1+s)/2, attained uniquely by normalized v+q. The traversed positive eigenvector arc gives the entire-interval bound. A complex row has constant multiplier for all c exactly at unit quadrature sensors (1,±i)/sqrt2; above 4/3 both eigenmodes appear on positive-measure fibers and any 1×2 row has a kernel. Independent Fourier-fiber numerical checks at ω=.05,.25,1,4/3 match sharp endpoints and verify the constant half-energy multiplier; these do not prove the infinite graph result.
